statement: For the mass threshold bc in Theorem 1.1, 0 < bc < ∞, m(bc) = 0, and the primary height coefficient of [Ope26b] satisfies a(bc) = 8π. (2.3) At a general positive coefficient a = a(b) > 0, the following statements hold. 1. On free rectangles tending after scaling to a fixed nondegenerate rectangle U, the tests ⟨h, AUN f(·/N)⟩, for smooth f near U, have joint Gaussian Laplace and moment limits with covariance a R U ∇f · ∇g, where the lattice mesh is N−1. Mean-free density smears have covariance a(−∆U,N )−1; bounded piecewise continuous densities and face smears, centered by a volume smear, are allowed. 2. In a fixed polygonal geometry made of finitely many rectangular pieces, with positive-width passages and box pin regions p, the corresponding limits have precision a−1 Z U |∇v|2 , v ∈ H1 (U), v = 0 on p. Free components are taken modulo constants. A fixed finite-rank nonnegative quadratic penalty in box averages gives the corresponding Gaussian penalty; if it controls all free constants, those constants are integrated in the limit. Bounded-step coherent rounding is permitted. 5 3. The fractional free mean modulo 2π tends to uniform measure, independently of the Gaussian observations. If um is the uniform probability on an m-square and tm is a zero-total profile of bounded reference cost, then for every fixed nonzero integer k, Eei⟨h,kum+tm⟩ −→ 0. Writing ρ̄m for the average of the four face probabilities and zm = Eei⟨h,ρ̄m⟩, one has lim inf m→∞ zGm zm ≥ cbG2−a/(4π) (2.4) for sufficiently large fixed integers G, with cb > 0 independent of G.
